project: Outlook Integrated Smart AI Project Management Dashboard

labels.name: MEETING
labels.definition: The current message schedules, confirms, changes, cancels, or substantively discusses a specific project meeting. A meeting may be in person or remote.

labels.name: DEADLINE
labels.definition: The current message states, sets, changes, confirms, or follows up on a date or time by which a project action or deliverable is due.

labels.name: REPORT_REQUEST
labels.definition: The current message requests preparation, submission, provision, or delivery of a report or another formal project document, including minutes, presentations, plans, and similar deliverables.

labels.name: DEPARTMENTAL_INPUT
labels.definition: The current message requests, tracks, or reports a project contribution, data, feedback, decision, or other input from a department or organizational unit.

labels.name: ACTION_REQUEST
labels.definition: The current message requests, directs, or assigns a concrete project task beyond a bare formal-document submission, departmental-input request, or approval transaction. It can co-occur when a distinct operational action is requested.

labels.name: FOLLOW_UP
labels.definition: The current message reminds, chases, checks, or escalates a previously expected or assigned project action, response, or deliverable. Thread context may establish that the action is a follow-up.

labels.name: APPROVAL
labels.definition: The current message requests, grants, rejects, withholds, or conditions formal project approval, sign-off, or authorization.

labels.name: GENERAL_UPDATE
labels.definition: The current message communicates a project status, progress, completion, blocker, decision, or change in work state. It may co-occur with any other project label.

labels.name: NON_PROJECT
labels.definition: The current message is outside the project-management email scope: it has no project meeting, deadline, document request, departmental input, action request, follow-up, approval, or project status/progress content. It is an internal filtering label.

rules: Assign every applicable project label independently; do not choose a single best class.
NON_PROJECT is exclusive: it cannot co-occur with any of the eight project labels.

An empty labels array means classification is unassigned or explicitly adjudicated outside the current inventory; it is never a negative training label. The unlabelled status requires labels=[] but may carry provisional source-mapped spans with annotation.annotation_source="dataset".
Use NON_PROJECT for reviewed out-of-scope emails. Do not use an empty array to encode NON_PROJECT.
Do not infer a label from a keyword alone; annotate the communicative function in context.

ACTION_REQUEST covers standalone project tasks. Do not add it solely because a report submission, departmental-input request, or approval request is phrased as an imperative; add it when a distinct operational task is requested.

span_labels.name: MEETING_DATE
span_labels.definition: The exact date or relative-date expression for a specific project meeting, as written (for example, '30 September' or 'next Friday'). Do not calculate or replace it with a normalized date.

span_labels.name: MEETING_TIME
span_labels.definition: The exact time expression for a specific project meeting, as written (for example, '3 PM' or 'between 10 and 11'). Keep the date in a separate MEETING_DATE span.

span_labels.name: DEADLINE_DATE
span_labels.definition: The exact date or relative-date expression that sets a project action or deliverable's due date (for example, 'Friday' or 'tomorrow'). Annotate a separate DEADLINE_TIME when a due time is also stated.

span_labels.name: DEADLINE_TIME
span_labels.definition: The exact clock-time, time-range, or conventional end-of-day expression for a due project action, such as '5 PM', '3 PM', or 'COB'. A date and time in the same sentence receive separate DEADLINE_DATE and DEADLINE_TIME spans.

span_labels.name: PARTICIPANT
span_labels.definition: A person or group explicitly named in the message as attending, invited to, or participating in a specific project meeting or project activity. Do not copy email recipients from metadata.

span_labels.name: RESPONSIBLE_PARTY
span_labels.definition: A person, role, or group explicitly assigned or committed to perform a project action. Annotate the textual person/group mention; do not infer names from sender/recipient metadata or annotate bare first-person pronouns.

span_labels.name: DEPARTMENT
span_labels.definition: The exact name of an organizational department or unit that supplies, owns, reviews, or is asked for a project input/action.

span_labels.name: AGENDA
span_labels.definition: A concise topical phrase explicitly identified as a subject for discussion at a project meeting. Do not write an inferred or generated summary.

span_labels.name: ACTION_ITEM
span_labels.definition: The shortest complete textual action phrase that is requested, assigned, committed to, or explicitly checked/followed up in the current message. Use thread context only to interpret the action; include its verb and necessary object, and exclude a separately expressed owner and deadline.

span_labels.name: REQUESTED_DOCUMENT
span_labels.definition: The exact name or type of a project document/material that is requested, expected, or being followed up in the current message (for example, 'revised budget report' or 'meeting minutes').

span_labels.name: PROJECT
span_labels.definition: An explicit project name, identifier, or unambiguous project title. Do not annotate generic references such as 'the project' without a specific name.

annotation_rules.content_for_labels: current_message, interpreted with subject, metadata, and thread_context where useful
annotation_rules.content_for_spans: current_message by default; subject only when span.field is 'subject'
annotation_rules.quoted_text: Do not assign labels or spans based only on quoted/forwarded earlier messages. Use thread_context to interpret the current message, not to copy prior actions into it.
annotation_rules.raw_text: Preserve raw_body. Annotation does not rewrite source fields.
annotation_rules.metadata: Use sender, recipients, cc, sent_at, thread_id, and attachment_names as supplied fields; do not create NLP spans for them.
annotation_rules.synthetic: Use source_dataset='synthetic'; synthetic records can never be gold and must not enter a gold test set.
annotation_rules.unlabelled: Classification labels must be empty. Provisional extraction spans mapped from source-dataset annotations are allowed only with annotation.annotation_source="dataset"; they are not human-reviewed or gold.
annotation_rules.dataset_mapped_spans: Keep only documented mappings whose text and offsets are verified. Human review must verify, correct, or remove every mapped span before setting status=human_reviewed and annotation_source=human.
annotation_rules.action_only: A reviewed project action-only email receives ACTION_REQUEST, not NON_PROJECT, GENERAL_UPDATE, or an empty label list.
annotation_rules.deadline_time: Annotate explicit due times separately as DEADLINE_TIME; do not infer a clock time from a date-only deadline.
